page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. This instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with 32 vCPUs, utilizing a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI) and AES cryptography.

The instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage solutions for persistent data. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. There are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The lack of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators represents a tradeoff, positioning this instance away from high-density local storage or heavy parallel graphics workloads.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge consistently within the average performance tier. In CPU-focused evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1436.68 and a multi-core score of 30666.35, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 11107.0. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 1705.41 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 109.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. For database and web operations, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 21.45 GB/sec and processed 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second. Qualitatively, the dedicated core allocation offers stable, non-burstable compute resources, making it a predictable option for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without the premium of GPU-accelerated hardware.

Based on its balanced 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU cores, this instance is configured for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, text processing, and medium-scale database operations. It is also capable of handling lightweight machine learning tasks, processing 45.98 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B LLM model.
